next_question: Does the OECD/COINr pipeline preserve feature-weighted density ranking on full DOM (not truncated-first-20) with richer element diversity — and does ranking stability improve when the sample contains more elements per definition, reducing the sensitivity to recipe sampling?
why_next: The MIXED verdict confirms the pipeline preserves discrimination (C3 PASS, eta2 ≫ 0.05) but ranking reversals under recipe sampling (C4 FAIL) prevent full validation. The truncated-first-20 sample with template-invariant within-type structure makes eta2 trivially achievable; the real test is ranking stability. Full DOM samples with richer element diversity would increase the fraction of discriminative elements captured by each definition, potentially reducing recipe-sampling sensitivity and stabilizing rankings. This is a materially orthogonal question from the current experiment (which tested pipeline structure) — it tests whether the observed ranking instability is a sample-size artifact or a structural limitation.

recommended_action: Design an experiment that tests feature-weighted density ranking stability on full DOM (not truncated-first-20) with richer element diversity. The truncated-first-20 sample with template invariance makes eta2 trivially achievable but ranking unstable under recipe sampling. Full DOM samples would increase the fraction of discriminative elements per definition, potentially stabilizing rankings. The experiment should: (1) use the full locatable_sample (not truncated-first-20) from EXP-INTEL-34782350557; (2) compute feature-weighted density for DEF-FULL-MAP and DEF-FORM-ONLY across all tasks; (3) test ranking preservation across canonical and per-task recipes with full 10×1000 sampling; (4) compare non-recipe vs recipe ranking agreement to quantify the sample-size effect. If ranking stabilizes on full DOM, the MIXED program is fully unblocked with feature-weighted density. If ranking remains unstable, the recipe-sensitivity is structural and product lane must use non-recipe density only.
